whatBypassesIt: PRIMARY: every real write path. The Cloud Run job actually writing parcel_record_cell right now is named 'factory-parcel-record-fill' in the runs table (confirmed live, section stepC). grep for that literal string, and reasonable camelCase/snake_case variants, across the entire hauska-engine repo returns zero files. Per canon-preamble, 'THE FACTORY (OPS-19, F- rows)... own repo hauska-factory... nothing reaches a serving store except through publish' -- the actual writer almost certainly lives in hauska-factory, not hauska-engine, which this dispatch explicitly instructed not to open. Reporting this rather than guessing: I cannot confirm from hauska-engine alone whether hauska-factory imports @hauska-engine/engine-core's publish-gate and calls it before considering a county published, or whether it writes parcel_record_cell directly via SQL with no reference to this library at all. That determination requires either a hauska-factory-side lane or an operator answer.

SECONDARY, confirmed by the gate's own test suite: 'poisoning the last earned cell of a rail demotes it (known limit)' -- if every earned cell (value/absent-verified/refused) on a given rail, across the whole record set being evaluated, is poisoned to unaccounted, deriveLiveRailKeys() (liveness.ts) reclassifies that rail as NOT live, and evaluatePublishGate excludes non-live ('declared-ahead') rails from scoring entirely. A rail that has gone from fully-sourced to 100% unaccounted therefore passes the gate silently, indistinguishable from a rail nobody ever attempted. This is named in the test file's own comment as a known, accepted limit, not a hidden defect -- but it is a real bypass path and belongs in this answer.
